title: Provenance-enriched evals alert stream with adaptive rate-limiting and grouping
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: surface high-confidence quality regressions detected by automated eval runs into the Console notification stream (Slack + PagerDuty) while minimizing noise via provenance-aware grouping and adaptive rate limiting. This ticket defines the data model, dedupe grouping heuristics, routing rules, and rollout plan for the first implementation.
background: We already run periodic eval batches and have alerting prototypes, but customers report noisy notifications after config/model rollouts where many similar failures are fired across routes and prompt-sets. Current dedupe is simplistic (exact-match on alert signature) and misses near-duplicates and related regressions caused by a single deployment. We need alerts that carry change provenance (who/what/when), group similar signals into a single actionable item, and throttle repeated noise while preserving fast paging for critical regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Console shows provenance-enriched alert with model/config fingerprint and links to the rollout that triggered the check
Slack messages are grouped: one consolidated thread per change fingerprint for the first 30 minutes
PagerDuty triggers only for grouped alerts classified as "critical" by severity rules (see severity matrix)
Deduplication groups alerts using similarity >= 0.8 over failing prompt sets and same change fingerprint
Adaptive rate limiting prevents more than 1 external notification per change fingerprint per 5 minutes after the first 30 minutes, configurable in Console
Telemetry captures grouped_alert_id and individual_signal_ids for investigation and rollback workflows
design_decisions: Compute a change_fingerprint combining model_version, config_hash, rollout_id, and route_id; use this as primary grouping key
Use weighted Jaccard similarity on failing prompt tokens (token-level shingles) to identify near-duplicate alerts; threshold = 0.80 initially
Preserve first-class failure examples in the Console UI with a collapse/expand experience: summary + top 5 representative prompts
Implement an adaptive quiet window: first 30 minutes allow summarized thread creation in Slack, after 30 minutes throttle to 1 external notify / 5 minutes per change_fingerprint
PagerDuty policy: immediate paging if severity = critical AND grouped_failure_ratio > 0.25 across evaluation suite; otherwise create an internal Console incident without paging
Expose grouping/rate-limit knobs in Console per-project and per-organization for enterprise customers
tradeoffs: Aggressive grouping reduces noise but can hide distinct regressions that co-occur; mitigated by including representative examples and allowing quick ungrouping in Console
Using a high similarity threshold reduces false grouping but may increase duplicate notifications; threshold will be tuned during canary
Computing token-shingle similarity is CPU work; we'll precompute failure signatures during eval ingestion and store them as compact bitsets to speed comparisons
Delaying PagerDuty pages reduces prompt paging fatigue but may delay urgent incident response; severity matrix aims to ensure critical regressions still page immediately
implementation_notes: Add change_fingerprint to eval-run event schema (ingestion service change) - ENG contract to publish to event bus
Create a new alert-grouping service that subscribes to eval events, computes similarity with recent signals (window = 48h), and emits grouped_alert records
Console API: GET /v1/evals/grouped_alerts and POST /v1/evals/grouped_alerts/actions for ack/unmute/unassign

Slack integration: post a thread root message with grouped_alert_id and attach a compact 'provenance card' (who, rollout link, failing-suite-stats). Follow-ups from #thread will be linked back to grouped_alert_id
PagerDuty integration: use event dedup key = grouped_alert_id and include runbook link and rollback playbook in payload
Telemetry: emit metrics grouped_alerts.created, grouped_alerts.merged, grouped_alerts.rate_limited, grouped_alerts.paged
Config in Console: per-org toggle for 'conservative grouping' vs 'aggressive grouping' and edit of similarity threshold and quiet windows
rollout_plan: Canary 1 (internal): Route alerts for 2 internal teams, similarity threshold = 0.80, quiet window = 30m -> monitor grouped_alerts.merged rate and Slack thread activity
Canary 2 (beta customers): add 3 pilot customers who opt into 'provenance alerts' feature; collect feedback and tune thresholds
Wide rollout: flip default to enabled for all customers with conservative defaults (threshold = 0.85, quiet window = 15m) and provide migration doc
Post-rollout review at 30d: evaluate signal-to-noise, PD paging volume, customer satisfaction surveys
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-grouping hides independent regressions -> mitigation: surface representative prompts and allow manual split/ungroup in Console
Risk: Increased CPU/memory from similarity computations -> mitigation: precompute signatures, limit comparison window to recent 48h, and use approximate set sketches
Risk: PagerDuty fatigue if rules misclassify severity -> mitigation: add a PD safelist and require two independent severity signals for auto-page in first 30d
Risk: Slack thread flood if many groups start simultaneously -> mitigation: global circuit breaker that silences non-critical groups if > N threads created in T minutes
metrics_and_alerts: Primary metrics: grouped_alerts.rate, grouped_alerts.merge_ratio, external_notifications.count (Slack/PagerDuty), pd_pages.count
SLOs: keep external_notifications.per_eval_run < 0.02 for non-critical regressions
Health alert: grouped_alerting.service_error_rate > 1% for 10m -> PagerDuty to SRE
Quality signals: post-rollout, track mean time to acknowledge for grouped alerts and mean time to rollback when provenance points to a recent rollout
ux_considerations: Console grouped alert card includes: title, change provenance (who, commit/rollout link, model_version, config_hash), top failing prompts (expandable), aggregated metrics (failure rate delta), and quick actions (re-run eval, mark as known-issue, create PD incident)
Slack message shows a short provenance line and a 'Open in Console' button that deep-links into the grouped alert thread
Provide a 'mute for this rollout' button in console and Slack to suppress further non-critical notifications for that change_fingerprint
